Addax 6.2.0 is a stabilization release: 38 fixes, features and refactors across the engine, the shared libraries, the plugins and the shipped scripts since 6.1.0, several of them closing paths that corrupted, dropped or silently truncated data, plus 23 dependency updates and a larger end-to-end suite (27 cases, up from 18). It also adds four capabilities — the server now runs every job in its own process, DuckDB gains a reader and a writer, the HTTP reader prefetches pages and the Elasticsearch writer kee

Highlights:
- `PosApiController::checkout()` now reuses `CheckoutService` instead of duplicating ~250 LOC of transaction creation, pricing, stock decrement, FEFO batch consumption, and receivable creation. API and web checkout now share the same code path through `CheckoutContext` DTO. Zero behavior change.
- Suite 354 tests pass (1556 assertions), Pint clean.

Breaking changes: none.

Upgrade steps: no migration required.

- Refactor: extracted ~250 LOC `DB::transaction` closure from `TransactionController::store()` into a dedicated `CheckoutService`. Controller now builds a `CheckoutContext` DTO, calls the service, and handles only post-commit side effects. Checkout core is now directly unit-testable.

- Multi-outlet architecture: outlets → warehouses → product_warehouse; one shared database, no tenants.
- Demo data split: production seed is system-only; `php artisan db:seed --class=DemoSeeder --force` (or `seed:demo --force`) loads the multi-outlet demo dataset.
- `php artisan db:seed --class=DemoSeeder --force` regenerates the four-outlet demo (PUSAT, MAL, TKB, PUT) with users assigned.

## Added
- Split payment with up to two tenders per transaction.
- Tender-level payment records and API resources.
- Gateway-specific split payment references and webhook aggregation.
- Split-tender receipt output and cash-aware shift summaries.

## Improved
- Transaction exports list the individual tender methods.
- Split refund UI clearly states the v1 cash-refund limitation.

## Upgrade
- Run `php artisan migrate` to create the `transaction_tenders` table.
- Split payment is online-only; offline sync rem
- Added migration for `cashier_shifts.cash_in_total` / `cash_out_total` — fresh installs and CI now match the shift-summary schema (previously only present on databases patched manually).

## Fixes

### 🧭 Guided tour corrections
- **Dashboard tour text fixed** — steps beyond the first showed raw i18n keys (`stats.title`, `chart.desc`, …) instead of real text; all steps now resolve the correct `tour.dashboard.*` strings.
- **No more error popup after tour** — completing or replaying a tour (and "Replay Guided Tours" in the user menu) used Inertia requests against JSON-only endpoints, triggering the *"All Inertia requests must receive a valid Inertia response"* popup. Both now use plai
- Added `docs/testing-manual.md` — a manual device-testing checklist (QRIS sandbox end-to-end, real ESC/POS printer, offline sync scenarios).

## Highlights

### 🖨️ True ESC/POS thermal printing (WebUSB)
- Raw ESC/POS byte generator built in — no heavy libraries: 58mm (32ch) and 80mm (48ch) widths, bold/center/right alignment, paper cut (GS V).
- **Connect Printer** flow in Settings > Printer: connect a USB receipt printer, run a Test Print, kick the cash drawer, disconnect.
- Drawer kick (ESC p) supported for standard pin-2 cash drawers.

### ⚡ Auto-print after checkout
- New behavior driven by existing printer settings (Settings > Print

## Highlights

### 💰 Shift cash in/out
- New `shift_cash_movements` table — record cash in (e.g. change float top-up) and cash out (petty cash withdrawal) during an active shift.
- Expected cash now accounts for movements: `opening_cash + cash sales − cash refunds + cash in − cash out`.
- Buttons on the active shift card; movements listed in shift detail.

### 🖨️ X/Z shift reports
- **X-report** (running shift) printable from the shift index; **Z-report** (final closing) from closed shift deta

## Highlights

### 🔄 Offline Transaction Sync (Phase 1)
- Offline queued transactions now actually sync. New batch endpoint `POST /api/v1/pos/transactions/sync` reuses the full server-side checkout flow (PricingService revalidation — client grand_total is always ignored).
- **Idempotency**: `transactions.client_uuid` (unique) prevents double-charging when the flush retries.
- Offline queue now captures item-level data (product_id, unit_id, qty) so queued sales can be checked out server-side.

`WithTemplate(version, build)` gives every test process (one per package under `go test ./...`) a database of its own, so `-p 1` is no longer needed.
- `WithSetup` runs on the worker every time (fixtures with relative dates), and `Cleaner.URL(ctx)` is the database to hand to code that opens its own connection.
- The schema is built once per version into a template database (`<name>_tpl_<hash>`), under an advisory lock, by whichever process comes first.
- A process leases the lowest free worker database (`<n

- `ScratchDatabase(t, adminURL)`: an empty, uniquely named database, dropped with the test.
- Strategies: `Transaction()` (go-txdb, nested transactions become savepoints), `Truncation()`, `Deletion()` (children before parents) and `Null()`, with `Only(...)` / `Except(...)`; migration tables are never touched.
First release: put a PostgreSQL database back to its baseline after each Go test, the way Ruby's DatabaseCleaner does.
